title: Sparse-burst qbatch policy proposal
content:
Purpose:
This note proposes a set of pragmatic batching + qcache + quantization rules specifically targeted at workloads characterized by low baseline throughput and frequent short-duration bursts ("sparse-burst" patterns). The goal is to reduce unit token cost while preserving 95th/99th percentile latency SLOs and avoiding model-accuracy regressions from aggressive quantization.

Context and problem statement:
- Observed pattern: long idle periods (minutes to hours) with occasional spikes of dozens-to-hundreds of concurrent short requests (single-digit to ~50 tokens). Common in search/autocomplete, form autofill, lightweight chat on low-traffic endpoints.
- Naive batching policies either: 1) wait too long to reach large batch sizes (hurting tail latency for spikes), or 2) flush quickly and fail to amortize GPU kernel overhead (higher per-token cost).
- QCache (prefix KV caching) helps when repeated prefixes are present, but sparse-burst traffic often has high unique prompt rate (few repeated prefixes), so naive cache retention wastes memory.
- Quantization can lower throughput cost, but lower-precision artifacts increase variance for short-context requests and may impact downstream safety classifiers.

Design goals:
1) Keep 95th/99th latency within SLO targets for burst windows (configurable per-route).
2) Reduce average token cost by 15-40% vs baseline small-batch eager flush.
3) Avoid increasing error/regression risk beyond a small, measurable delta for quality metrics.
4) Simple server-side policy knobs that product teams can tune without per-model retraining.

High-level policy summary (proposal):
A. Adaptive two-mode batching (fast-path and economy-path)
  - Fast-path: low-latency mode used when p95 latency risk is high (detected via route flag or recent tail spikes). Parameters: max_wait_ms=6-10ms, max_batch_tokens=512, batch_size_cap=8. Use this when request concurrency <= 30 and median prompt length < 40 tokens.
  - Economy-path: during sustained bursts with >30 concurrent inflight requests or when GPU utilization > 45% for >15s, switch to economy-path: larger batch windows with max_wait_ms=25-40ms, batch_size_cap=64, max_batch_tokens=4096. Aggressively aggregate short requests to amortize kernel overhead.
  - Hysteresis: require conditions to persist for 10s before switching modes to avoid oscillation. Manual override via route config.

B. Burst-aware batching heuristics
  - Token-aware grouping: prioritize grouping short requests together but enforce a per-batch max_token ratio to avoid single long request blocking batch progress. For example, if a long request > 512 tokens arrives, it is isolated unless the batch reaches >75% of token capacity with other short requests.
  - Admission control: temporarily delay low-priority background inference by up to 50ms during peak bursts (policy per customer).

C. QCache retention and eviction policies for sparse-burst
  - Short TTL for unique prefixes: default prefix cache TTL=30s for routes with >50% unique prefix rate; otherwise 120s.
  - Hotset detection: maintain small LRU window (size proportional to recent concurrency, e.g., 4 * median concurrent requests) to hold active prefixes during bursts.
  - Prefix similarity grouping: if exact-prefix hit rate < 10% but high lexical overlap exists (same template with variable slots), enable lightweight template hashing to increase effective cache reuse.

D. Quantization profiles and fallback rules
  - Model families: profile quantization sensitivity per-model (e.g., Llama2-13B, mix-8, Mistral variants). Use three tiers: conservative (int8 but per-matrix dynamic), standard (4-bit QAT/GPTQ tuned), aggressive (4-bit fastpath with extra calibration).
  - Route-level quantization: default to conservative for user-facing short-prompt routes. Allow standard/aggressive for non-critical internal batch jobs.
  - Runtime A/B gating: enable canary quantized variant for 1% of traffic with automatic rollback if quality delta > threshold (configured by eval harness).

E. Pre-warming and resource hints
  - Burst pre-warm: when telemetry detects increasing inbound rate (exponential moving average, span 10s), pre-warm dedicated small worker(s) at quantized tier to reduce cold-start tail. Cost vs latency tradeoff is exposed as a simple toggle in route config.
  - Warmed KV-cache snapshot restore: for private deployments, provide option to snapshot active qcache hotset and restore on new workers to minimize warmup.

Cost model spreadsheet: recommended minimal layout for rapid estimation
Columns (one row per scenario):
  - scenario_name
  - concurrency_pattern (sparse | steady | bursty)|
  - median_prompt_tokens
  - percent_short_requests (<=32 tokens)
  - batching_mode_used (fast | economy)
  - avg_batch_size_requests
  - avg_batch_tokens
  - tokens_per_second_per_gpu
  - gpu_hours_per_day
  - cost_per_gpu_hour
  - quant_profile (conservative | standard | aggressive)
  - estimated_unit_cost_per_1k_tokens
  - p95_latency_ms
  - quality_delta_pct
Suggested formulas (spreadsheet-friendly):
  - avg_batch_tokens = median_prompt_tokens * avg_batch_size_requests
  - tokens_per_second_per_gpu = (avg_batch_tokens * batches_per_second_per_gpu) where batches_per_second_per_gpu = 1 / (avg_batch_latency_ms / 1000)
  - gpu_hours_per_day = total_tokens_per_day / (tokens_per_second_per_gpu * 3600)
  - estimated_unit_cost_per_1k_tokens = (gpu_hours_per_day * cost_per_gpu_hour) / (total_tokens_per_day / 1000)
Notes on inputs: batches_per_second_per_gpu should model kernel latency + queueing; use conservative numbers for tail-sensitive routes.

Quick recommended defaults to try (start here for experiments):
- Short-feedback search route (median 12 tokens, bursty spikes to 120 concurrent): start with fast-path: max_wait_ms=8, batch_size_cap=12, qcache_ttl=30s, quant_profile=conservative. Expected ~10-20% cost reduction vs immediate-flush baseline with negligible p95 change.
- Low-priority analytics route (median 40 tokens, sustained 500 RPS): economy-path: max_wait_ms=30, batch_size_cap=64, qcache_ttl=120s, quant_profile=standard. Expected ~30-40% cost reduction, modest p95 increase.

Operational checklist for rollout (short):
1) Add route-level flags: burst_detection_threshold, hyst_time_s, default_batch_policy, qcache_ttl_policy, quant_canary_pct.
2) Implement simulator run: replay production traces for 24h using proposed logic and capture cost + latency + quality. Generate two spreadsheet scenarios (baseline, proposed).
3) Canary: deploy to 1% traffic for 6h, run black-box quality checks and p95 monitoring.
4) Ramp to 25% for 24–48h if no regressions, then full roll.
5) Post-roll: schedule 7-day cost/quality review and a regression alert to auto-roll back if quality delta > X or p99 spike > Y.

Open questions and risks:
- Template/hash-based qcache grouping requires lightweight parsing; might fail on very freeform prompts. Need to define safe heuristics and opt-out per route.
- Quantization regression risk for short-context classification is under-explored; require per-model small eval suites derived from customer prompts.
- Pre-warm cost: how many standby workers are acceptable? Recommend making pre-warm optional per-customer with soft budget limits.

Next steps (immediate):
- Owner: Maya Patel. Engineering spike: 2 engineer-weeks to instrument simulator and run on 7 representative traces.
- Data: product to provide three canonical route traces (search, autofill, background analytics) and target SLOs.
- Deliverables: simulator results spreadsheet + canary config PR + short runbook for on-call.

Appendix: quick glossary of knobs referenced:
- max_wait_ms: maximum time a batch will wait for additional requests before flush.
- batch_size_cap: request-count cap per batch.
- max_batch_tokens: token-cap per batch to bound memory and latency.
- qcache_ttl: time-to-live for prefix cache entries.
- quant_profile: pre-defined quantization configuration with known perf/quality tradeoffs.

End of proposal.

(Please push feedback inline; planning to iterate after simulator results.)
